name: Leonardo da Vinci
story_childhood:
Leonardo was born on April 15, 1452,
 in a small village called Vinci, in Italy.

He loved to wander through the hills and watch the birds.

While other children played, he asked questions about everything.

He wanted to understand how the world worked.
story_takeaway: Stay curious, and the whole world becomes your workshop.
modern_interpretation:
If Leonardo were ten years old today, he'd probably have a tablet stuffed with drawings, a drawer full of half-built gadgets, and a hundred browser tabs open at once. He'd film slow-motion videos of water drops, design flying machines in 3D, and ask his teachers questions they couldn't quite answer.

He'd remind us that art and science aren't opposites — they're two ways of looking closely at the same wonderful world.

chapters.title: A Curious Child
chapters.narrative:
Leonardo noticed things
others did not see.

The patterns in leaves.
The shape of clouds.
The way water moved
around rocks.

Sometimes people thought
he was strange.
He didn't mind.
He kept asking anyway.

chapters.title: The Notebooks of Wonder
chapters.narrative:
Leonardo filled thousands of pages with his ideas. He wrote them in mirror-writing, backwards, so you needed a looking-glass to read them. On those pages he drew flying machines with flapping wings, a diving suit, a giant crossbow, and even a kind of helicopter — hundreds of years before engines existed.

He studied how muscles moved and how the heart pumped blood. He mapped rivers and imagined bridges. Most of his machines were never built in his lifetime, but they showed a mind that refused to believe anything was impossible — only 'not yet figured out.'

chapters.title: A Smile That Never Fades
chapters.narrative:
Leonardo painted slowly, because he wanted everything to be perfect. For a wall in Milan he created The Last Supper, capturing the exact moment a room full of friends turned to one another in surprise. And on a small poplar panel he painted a woman with a quiet, mysterious smile — the Mona Lisa.

He softened her edges with feather-light layers of paint, a trick he had invented by watching how shadows blur in real life. Centuries later, people still travel across the world just to stand before her and wonder what she is thinking.

chapters.title: The Wandering Master
chapters.narrative:
As the years passed, Leonardo travelled from city to city — Milan, Venice, Rome — designing waterways, festivals, and machines of war and wonder. Kings and dukes wanted his genius near them.

At last, a young French king invited him to live in a manor in France, where he could think and draw in peace. There, surrounded by his beloved notebooks, the old master kept sketching and questioning until the very end. He left the world far richer than he found it — not because he finished everything he started, but because he dared to imagine so much.

timeline.caption: Born near the town of Vinci, in Italy.
Becomes an apprentice in Verrocchio's Florence workshop.
Moves to Milan to serve as an artist and engineer.
Dies in France, his notebooks full of unfinished dreams.

lessons.lesson: Ask 'why?' about everything — even the ordinary things.
Look closely; the answers are often hiding in plain sight.
Great work takes time, so don't rush what matters.
Dream up what doesn't exist yet, then try to build it.
